summary: Koshu Itabashi (1927–2020) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sendai Daiichi High School (~1940–1944), the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy (~1944–1945), and Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Teruji Ishizu.

Kosuke Nakazawa (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held positions at Rissho University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he studied under Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at Hokkaido University (~1968–1991) and Sapporo Otani Junior College (1992).

Kotetsu Yoshida (b. 1941) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1926 to 1929 and served on the faculty at Taisho University from ~1952 to 1975.

Koun Yamada (1907–1989) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at First Higher School, he studied under Konan Sokan, Sogen Asahina, Kanzui Hanamoto, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, whom he succeeded from 1961 to 1989 after founding Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953.
Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (~1904–1933) and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After earning his master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Nishogakusha University (1965) and Toyo University (assistant professor in 1972; professor emeritus 1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai in 1893.

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Gakushuin, Kyoritsu Gakusha, and under Eun Maeda, served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914), and founded Kojukai in 1919.
Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He held an academic post at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and was attested there again in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indology scholar. He studied at Sanskrit College and University (~1853–1857) and Presidency University (~1857–1860), later holding posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist educated at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and as Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College, Kolkata, and studying under Alexander Duff, he held posts at Hare School (~1829–1831) and Bishop's College (1852).
Krishna Sharma is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She served as Principal of Gargi College and held an appointment as a Visiting Scholar at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held posts at Panjab University, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, Adyar Library, and founded the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation (attested 1997), and Upakulapati of Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (attested 1997).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism (both attested 2021).
